findings.description: The added `.strip()` removes all leading and trailing whitespace from the prompt, not just the ANSI codes that the change is meant to strip. A prompt such as "Name: " is passed to input() as "Name:", so the cursor sits directly against the colon.
findings.rationale: Trigger: a prompt whose text ends in a space (the usual form, e.g. click.prompt("Name", default=...) builds "Name: ") while should_strip_ansi is true, such as stdout piped or under CliRunner. The changed line strips the text, so func receives text without the trailing space. Impact: the rendered prompt loses its separator space and the output differs from the non-stripping path, so tests and users see a changed prompt.
